title: Business Trip Checklist
metaTitle: Business Trip Packing Checklist (Work Travel) | Gisti
metaDescription: A business trip packing checklist: laptop and adapters, wrinkle-free outfits, presentation tech, and travel-size toiletries. Free to use, or tailor it with AI in Gisti.
cardDesc: Laptop and adapters, wrinkle-free outfits, presentation tech, and the work-travel essentials.
intro: A business trip lives or dies by the tech and the outfits. Forget the presentation adapter or turn up in a creased shirt and the whole trip feels off. This checklist keeps your work travel sharp: everything for the meeting, the flight, and the hotel. See more travel checklists.

items.text: Photo ID or passport and any visa needed
Boarding passes, hotel, and rental-car confirmations
Laptop, charger, and a spare charging cable
Phone, power bank, and adapter for your destination
Notebook and pens, or a tablet and stylus
Two or three wrinkle-resistant business outfits
items.note: Hang them the moment you arrive.

items.text: One smart-casual outfit for dinners or downtime
Comfortable dress shoes you've already worn in
Toiletries and a grooming kit in travel sizes
Presentation dongles and an HDMI or USB-C adapter
items.note: Hotels and clients rarely have the right cable.

items.text: Printed copies of key documents as a backup
Reusable water bottle and a few snacks
Noise-cancelling headphones for the flight and the hotel
Expense receipts folder or app set up before you go

items.note: Hotel outlets are always in short supply.

items.text: A light layer for cold conference rooms and planes

faq.q: What should I pack for a business trip?
faq.a: Your laptop and all its adapters, phone and power bank, two-to-three wrinkle-resistant business outfits, comfortable dress shoes, business cards, presentation dongles, and travel-size toiletries. A multi-port charger solves the always-too-few hotel outlets.

faq.q: How do I pack business clothes without wrinkles?
faq.a: Roll knits and fold structured items along their seams, use the hotel's hangers as soon as you arrive, and hang garments in the bathroom during a hot shower to steam out creases. Wrinkle-resistant fabrics and a garment folder help most.

faq.q: What tech should I not forget for a work trip?
faq.a: The easily-forgotten items are the presentation adapter (HDMI or USB-C), a spare charging cable, a power bank, and a small multi-port charger. Clients and hotels rarely have the exact cable you need, so bring your own.
